subject: Merging chromosomes in de novo linkage map?

messages.author: 1220f7a833c6ec8b
messages.subject: Merging chromosomes in de novo linkage map?
parts:
Hi,

Sorry if this is a repeat question, but you've mentioned a few times that when making a de novo linkage map you usually start off with more linkage groups than chromosomes and then merge them later. When do you merge them relative to other steps (e.g. est.rf, orderMarkers)? How do you make the decision which groups to merge? I currently have about 2.3x as many linkage groups as I expect to have chromosomes, and about 1/3 of those linkage groups are singletons. I'm happy to provide more data if it'll help!

Thanks so much,

Joanna Rifkin

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Merging chromosomes in de novo linkage map?
parts:
Unfortunately, I don't have any specific advice other than what's presented in the tutorial on genetic map construction, http://rqtl.org/tutorials/geneticmaps.pdf

You often end up with a bunch of singletons (single markers that don't show linkage to any others); those may be badly behaved markers that won't ever be able to fit into a map, so I would discount those.

karl
